title: Deterministic generalized k-server: tower lower bound and strict upper bound
abstract: For generalized k-server, each named server moves in its own metric space, a request specifies one point per space, and matching any coordinate serves the request. The development proves a height-k tower lower bound on the deterministic competitive ratio on k real lines for k at least three, allowing arbitrary additive constants. It also proves existence of a lazy deterministic algorithm on arbitrary metric spaces with arbitrary positive movement weights and prescribed initial configuration, with an explicit factor depending only on k and no additive cost or horizon input. The refined deterministic factor is at most tower(k+4) for k at least two.
